defect.snippet: customFields: ticket.customFields as unknown as Record<string, string>,

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how tickets are converted to and from their JSON representation? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: In toDto, customFields is a Map cast to Record. The cast only silences the compiler; JSON.stringify serializes a Map as {} because it has no own enumerable properties. Every GET and PATCH response therefore returns "customFields": {} even though the data is stored correctly (patchTicket uses Object.fromEntries for the DB row). It should be Object.fromEntries(ticket.customFields).

choiceQuestions.prompt: A row is stored with priority "critical". What happens on GET /tickets/:id?
choices: 500, because fromRow throws on unknown priorities
choiceQuestions.explanation: fromRow checks the value against PRIORITIES and falls back to "normal" when it is not listed, so the response is 200 with "normal". It does not throw, pass the raw value through, or produce a 422.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A PATCH body contains {"addTags": ["Billing", "billing"]} on a ticket with no tags. What tags does the stored row end up with?
choiceQuestions.explanation: applyPatch lowercases each tag and adds it to a Set, so both collapse to a single "billing"; patchTicket spreads the Set into an array. Nothing preserves case, keeps duplicates, or rejects the request.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does applyPatch build next with new Set(ticket.tags) and new Map(ticket.customFields) instead of relying on the spread alone?
choices: Spread converts Set and Map into plain arrays
Spread copies references, so mutating next.tags would also mutate the original ticket's collections
Spread throws on Set and Map
It is needed so JSON.stringify can serialize them
choiceQuestions.explanation: Object spread is shallow: next.tags would be the same Set instance as ticket.tags, and add/set/delete would alter the input. Copying the collections keeps the original unmodified. Spread does not convert or throw, and the copies have nothing to do with JSON output.
